title: KDRSolvers: Scalable, Flexible, Task-Oriented Krylov Solvers
problem: Sparse linear solver frameworks (PETSc, Trilinos) are inflexible in data partitioning; changes to partitioning strategies require extensive code refactoring and don't automatically propagate.
motivation: Krylov methods require flexible partitioning for optimal load balancing on heterogeneous systems; manual tuning for each new partition strategy wastes developer time and introduces bugs.
method: Abstract sparse matrix representation using dependent partitioning that maps between domain, range, and nonzero entries. Universal co-partitioning operators for matrices and vectors. Multi-operator systems enable non-contiguous data processing. Targets Legion task-based runtime system.
key_novelty: First abstraction to decouple sparse matrix storage format from Krylov algorithm implementation; automatic partitioning strategy propagation; multi-operator data ingestion.
contributions: Dependent partitioning abstraction for sparse matrix representation
Universal co-partitioning operators independent of storage format
Multi-operator systems for non-contiguous data processing
Competitive performance vs PETSc/Trilinos (9.6% time reduction on 1,024 GPUs)
limitations: Speedup modest (9.6%); Legion runtime overhead not isolated; scalability beyond 1,024 GPUs not tested; limited evaluation on diverse problem types.
primary_theme: Flexible sparse linear solvers via abstraction-based partitioning
